items.title: Section: Which Afflictions Generate Karma, and the Three Conditions for a Fall

items.zh: 問：貪等十煩惱幾能發業？幾不能發？答：一切能發。若諸煩惱猛利現行，方能發起往惡趣業，非諸失念而現行者。又分別起能發此業，非任運起。
items.en: Question: among the ten afflictions, greed and the rest, how many can generate karma, and how many cannot? Answer: all can generate it. Only when these afflictions manifest with force and vehemence are they able to generate karma leading to the evil destinies, never when they manifest merely through a lapse of mindfulness. Also, it is discrimination-arisen affliction that can generate this karma, not affliction arising spontaneously.

items.title: Section: Three Marks Every Affliction Shares

items.zh: 問：諸煩惱有幾相？答：略有三相。一、自相，二、共相，三、差別相。自相者，謂貪瞋等各各自性所攝相。共相者，謂諸煩惱無有差別，一切皆同不寂靜相。
items.en: Question: how many marks does affliction have? Answer: in brief, three. First, its own particular mark. Second, its mark held in common. Third, its distinguishing mark. Its own particular mark is whatever nature belongs specifically to greed, hatred, and the rest, each falling under its own essential character. Its mark held in common is that all afflictions, without distinction, share alike the single mark of being without inner stillness.

items.title: Section: Twenty-Six Names, Seven Angles — Affliction's Distinguishing Marks

items.zh: 差別相者，復有二種。一、門差別相，二、轉差別相。門差別相者，謂結、縛、隨眠、隨煩惱、纏等，如本地分已說。轉差別相者，謂隨眠轉故、所緣轉故、現行轉故、品差別轉故、力無力轉故、因果轉故、迷行轉故。
items.en: The distinguishing mark is further of two kinds. First, the gate-distinguishing mark. Second, the turning-distinguishing mark. The gate-distinguishing mark refers to knot, bond, latent tendency, secondary affliction, entanglement, and so forth, as already explained in the Basic Section. The turning-distinguishing mark refers to the turning of latent tendency, the turning of its object, the turning of manifestation, the turning of grade-differentiation, the turning of force or forcelessness, the turning of cause and effect, and the turning of confused conduct.

items.title: Section: Eighteen Kinds of Latent Tendency, and Who Can Never Be Severed of Them

items.zh: 復次，隨眠轉相略有十八。一、隨逐自境隨眠，二、隨逐他境隨眠，三、被損隨眠，四、不被損隨眠，五、隨增隨眠，六、不隨增隨眠，七、具分隨眠，八、不具分隨眠，九、可害隨眠，十、不可害隨眠，十一、增上隨眠，十二、平等隨眠，十三、下劣隨眠，十四、覺悟隨眠，十五、不覺悟隨眠，十六、能生多苦隨眠，十七、能生少苦隨眠，十八、不能生苦隨眠。隨逐自境隨眠者，謂三界中自地所攝隨眠。隨逐他境隨眠者，謂生上下地，下上煩惱所逐隨眠。被損隨眠者，謂世間離欲下地隨眠。不被損隨眠者，謂已離欲、或未離欲自地隨眠。隨增隨眠者，謂自地隨眠。不隨增隨眠者，謂他地隨眠。具分隨眠者，謂諸異生所有隨眠。不具分隨眠者，謂諸有學非異生者所有隨眠。可害隨眠者，謂般涅槃法所有隨眠。不可害隨眠者，謂不般涅槃法所有隨眠。
items.en: Moreover, the turning of latent tendency is, in brief, of eighteen kinds. First, latent tendency pursuing one's own realm. Second, latent tendency pursuing another realm. Third, damaged latent tendency. Fourth, undamaged latent tendency. Fifth, increasing latent tendency. Sixth, non-increasing latent tendency. Seventh, complete latent tendency. Eighth, incomplete latent tendency. Ninth, destructible latent tendency. Tenth, indestructible latent tendency. Latent tendency pursuing one's own realm is that belonging to one's own ground within the three realms. Latent tendency pursuing another realm is that of the lower or higher afflictions still following one born into a higher or lower ground. Damaged latent tendency is the latent tendency of a lower ground freed of desire through a mundane path. Undamaged latent tendency is the latent tendency of one's own ground, whether already freed of desire or not yet freed. Increasing latent tendency is latent tendency of one's own ground. Non-increasing latent tendency is latent tendency of another ground. Complete latent tendency is all the latent tendency belonging to ordinary beings. Incomplete latent tendency is the latent tendency belonging to noble learners who are not ordinary beings. Destructible latent tendency is the latent tendency of those with the potential for final nirvana. Indestructible latent tendency is the latent tendency of those without the potential for final nirvana.

items.title: Section: Waking and Sleeping Seeds — Completing the Eighteen

items.zh: 增上隨眠者，謂貪等行所有隨眠。平等隨眠者，謂等分行所有隨眠。下劣隨眠者，謂薄塵行所有隨眠。覺悟隨眠者，謂諸纏果與纏俱轉隨眠。不覺悟隨眠者，謂離諸纏而恒隨逐隨眠。能生多苦隨眠者，謂欲界隨眠。能生少苦隨眠者，謂色無色界隨眠。不能生苦隨眠者，謂得自在菩薩所有隨眠。
items.en: Superior latent tendency is the latent tendency belonging to those whose conduct is dominated by craving and the like. Equal latent tendency is the latent tendency belonging to those of evenly balanced conduct. Inferior latent tendency is the latent tendency belonging to those whose conduct carries only a thin dust of affliction. Awakened latent tendency is the latent tendency that is itself the fruit of manifest affliction, turning together with that manifestation. Unawakened latent tendency is the latent tendency that, apart from any manifestation, still constantly follows along. Latent tendency generating much suffering is the latent tendency of the desire realm. Latent tendency generating little suffering is the latent tendency of the form and formless realms. Latent tendency generating no suffering is the latent tendency belonging to bodhisattvas who have attained mastery.

items.title: Section: Why an Arhat's Body Still Differs From Their Own Severed Seeds

items.zh: 問：如說麁重體性名隨眠，此煩惱品麁重望彼諸行。當言有異？為不異耶？答：當言有異。何以故？由阿羅漢永害一切煩惱麁重，而諸行相續猶未斷絕故。問：有幾麁重攝諸麁重？答：略有十八。一、自性異熟麁重，二、自性煩惱麁重，三、自性業麁重，四、煩惱障麁重，五、業障麁重，六、異熟障麁重，七、蓋麁重，八、不正尋思麁重，九、愁惱麁重，十、怖畏麁重，十一、劬勞麁重，十二、飲食麁重，十三、眠夢麁重，十四、婬欲麁重，十五、界不平等麁重，十六、時分變異麁重，十七、終沒麁重，十八、遍行麁重。
items.en: Question: as it is said that the very nature of coarse-heaviness is called latent tendency, does this affliction-class coarse-heaviness differ from those conditioned formations, or not? Answer: it should be said that they differ. Why? Because an arhat has permanently destroyed every affliction-class coarse-heaviness, and yet the continuity of those conditioned formations has still not been cut off. Question: how many kinds of coarse-heaviness comprise every coarse-heaviness there is? Answer: in brief, eighteen. First, intrinsic ripening-coarseness. Second, intrinsic affliction-coarseness. Third, intrinsic karma-coarseness. Fourth, affliction-hindrance coarseness. Fifth, karma-hindrance coarseness. Sixth, ripening-hindrance coarseness. Seventh, coarseness of the obstructions. Eighth, coarseness of improper discursive thought. Ninth, coarseness of sorrow and distress. Tenth, coarseness of fear. Eleventh, coarseness of toilsome exertion. Twelfth, coarseness of food and drink. Thirteenth, coarseness of sleep and dreams. Fourteenth, coarseness of sexual desire. Fifteenth, coarseness of elemental imbalance. Sixteenth, coarseness of the changes of time. Seventeenth, coarseness of dying. Eighteenth, coarseness that is pervasive.

items.title: Section: From the Five Heinous Crimes to "No Samadhi in Old Age"

items.en: Karma-hindrance coarseness refers to the five heinous deeds, killing one's father, killing one's mother, killing an arhat, causing schism in the harmonious community, and shedding a buddha's blood, which leave a being without the capacity to cultivate calming and insight or attain the noble path. Ripening-hindrance coarseness is coarseness in the ripened result, the coarseness of one's fulfilling karma. Coarseness of the obstructions refers to the meaning of covering. Coarseness of improper discursive thought refers to improper thinking, discrimination not in accord with reason. Coarseness of the changes of time refers to ageing and decline; when old, body and mind decline and no longer follow the will as they once did, and so it is said that there is no samadhi in old age. Pervasive coarseness is the suffering of formations. It should be known that it pervades pleasant feeling, painful feeling, and neutral feeling alike. Such coarseness should be understood as already explained before.

items.title: Section: Seven Ways a Confused Mind Moves

items.zh: 復次，所緣、現行二轉，於其自處當廣宣說。品差別轉，當知如前蘊善巧說。力無力轉，當知如前本地分說。因果轉者，謂煩惱、業、生，皆以煩惱為因。果亦如是，隨應當知。欲界一分不善煩惱，有異熟果。應知所餘，無異熟果。迷行轉者，如本地分七種已列。義別云何？謂薩迦耶見、邊執見、邪見，此三於所知境起邪了行，於四聖諦迷行轉故。無明一種，是不了行。疑，是了不了行。
items.en: Moreover, the turning of object and the turning of manifestation shall be explained extensively in their own proper place. The turning of grade-differentiation should be understood as already explained under the skilful understanding of the aggregates. The turning of force and forcelessness should be understood as already explained in the Basic Section. The turning of cause and effect is that affliction, karma, and rebirth all take affliction as their cause, and the result should likewise be understood accordingly. The portion of desire-realm affliction that is unwholesome has a ripened result; the rest should be known to have no ripened result. The turning of confused conduct is as the seven kinds already listed in the Basic Section. Self-view, extreme-view, and wrong view, these three, generate wrongly understanding conduct with respect to what is known, being confused with respect to the four noble truths. Ignorance alone is failing-to-understand conduct. Doubt is uncertainly-understanding conduct.

blocks.text: Fascicle 59 continues the study of affliction: how it creates karma, its many names, and its latent forms.

All ten can generate karma, but karma leading to the lower realms requires force and discrimination. Master Cháng Bǎi: a passing lapse of mindfulness is easily noticed and treated; even noble ones lose mindfulness at times, yet they never go to the lower realms.
Master Cháng Bǎi: if the mind is not still, there is affliction; with affliction the mind cannot be still.
Master Cháng Bǎi: different names are given according to how affliction goes in and out and how it varies.

Master Cháng Bǎi: beings are followed by their own realm's seeds; even born in a higher realm, one is still followed by desire-realm seeds. Ordinary beings have all; learners lack those already severed.

subs.head: Thin dust, and the fruit of the active

blocks.text: Master Cháng Bǎi: 薄塵 means slight affliction. Latent tendency is called "the fruit of the active" because active affliction plants it.
Master Cháng Bǎi: the seeds of affliction in the store-consciousness are wholly severed, yet the present result of past heaviness, the five aggregates, lives on.
Master Cháng Bǎi: affliction arising spontaneously with lost mindfulness, without discrimination, has no force. Ignorance simply does not understand; doubt half understands.
Even noble ones lose mindfulness, but they "never go to the lower realms". A lapse noticed and corrected is not a fall.

quiz.q: How many of the ten afflictions generate karma, and which generate karma towards evil destinies?
options: only greed, hatred, and delusion; those of lapsed mindfulness and spontaneous arising
only the five views; those arising spontaneously
none can; only evil karma itself generates karma
all can; only forceful, discrimination-arisen ones generate karma towards evil destinies
quiz.why: All ten can generate karma, but karma towards the evil destinies requires force and discrimination. Master Cháng Bǎi: only when these ten, craving and view afflictions alike, manifest with great force can they generate karma leading to the three evil paths. The English here follows the Chinese.

quiz.q: Noble ones also have lapses. Why do they not fall, per Master Cháng Bǎi?
options: a lapse is easily noticed and treated; noble ones with lapses surely do not fall
noble ones never lapse, no affliction manifesting
their lapses are wholesome
they are all born in the higher realms
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: a passing loss of mindfulness with affliction is easily noticed and treated; even noble ones at times lose mindfulness, yet they certainly do not go to the three evil paths. So the question of a fall depends on force and on deliberate discrimination, not on the mere arising of affliction.

quiz.q: What is the common mark of all afflictions?
options: all alike lead to evil destinies, every affliction surely causing a fall, which the treatise regards as what they share
all alike are unwholesome
all alike have the mark of being without stillness
all alike are severed by vision
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: if the mind is not still there is surely affliction, and with affliction the mind cannot be still; deluded thought and distraction obstruct absorption and the path, and this is the common mark. The upper realms' afflictions are neutral, so unwholesomeness cannot be the shared mark.

quiz.q: What are affliction's three marks, and what is its own mark?
options: own, common, and distinguishing; each one's own nature
own, other, and joint marks
vision, cultivation, and adept; the results of greed
manifestation, latency, heaviness; seeds of latency
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: in brief, affliction has three aspects, own, common, and distinguishing; the own mark is the nature each of greed, hatred, and the others has. The English "its own particular mark" and "held in common" render these clearly.

quiz.q: How do the gate and turning distinctions differ, and what does 門 mean?
options: 門 is a Dharma method and 轉 the transformed basis, both concerning antidotes rather than affliction's own distinctions
a gate is where affliction goes in and out; turning is the differences in its arising
gates are faculties; turning is consciousness
the gate of hell; turning is saṃsāra
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: a gate is the place where affliction goes in and out; turning is the varied differences in affliction's arising. Different names are set according to different traits, such as knot and bond. The English "gate-distinguishing mark" is literal but fair.

quiz.q: What are latent tendencies pursuing one's own and another's realm?
options: desire-realm ones are one's own and the higher ones another's
severed ones are own; unsevered are another's
inward are own; outward are another's
those of one's own ground; those of other grounds following one born there
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: beings in the three realms are followed by their own ground's seeds; though born in the form or formless realm, one is still followed by desire-realm seeds. The English "realm" for 境 is loose but workable, the Chinese speaking of grounds.

quiz.q: What is damaged latent tendency, and why is increasing tendency only of one's own ground?
options: only those severed at vision are damaged; increasing means higher seeds, strengthened by absorption, while own-ground seeds shrink
worldly detachment damages lower-ground seeds; only own-ground seeds are repeatedly reinforced
latency when injured; growing with age
latency harmed by others; growing with giving
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: through the worldly path one cultivates absorption, leaves desire-realm desire, and attains the first absorption; only one's own ground's affliction seeds are repeatedly reinforced and grow stronger. "Damaged" is suppressed, not severed.

quiz.q: To whom belong complete, incomplete, destructible, and indestructible latent tendencies?
options: learners; ordinary beings; those without potential; those with
ordinary beings; noble learners; those with nirvāṇa potential; those without
bodhisattvas; hearers; solitary realisers; buddhas
desire; form; formless; nirvāṇa
quiz.why: Ordinary beings have all; noble learners lack those already severed. Master Cháng Bǎi: learners from the first fruit to the approach to arhatship still have unsevered innate seeds in the store-consciousness. Indestructible refers to those without nirvāṇa potential.

quiz.q: The English has "those of thin, dust-like conduct." What is the problem?
options: 塵 means affliction, which is thin; conduct is not dust-like, and the phrase makes no sense
no problem: conduct as thin as dust describes light behaviour, the English keeping the image, as the lecture does
the problem is "thin," which should be "thick"
the problem is "conduct," which should be "clothing"
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: 薄 means slight and 塵 means affliction; the seeds of one whose afflictions are slight are inferior latent tendency. So it is the defilement that is thin. "Dust-like conduct" attaches the image to the wrong word; "conduct of thin defilement" would be better.

quiz.q: The English has "whose manifestation-fruit turns together with its own manifestation." What is wrong?
options: nothing: 纏果 is the fruit borne by latency, manifest affliction
"turns" should be "stops"
纏果 is the latent tendency itself, born of manifestation; "whose" gives latency a separate fruit
"Awakened" should be "Buddha"
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: 纏果 means affliction seeds, that is, the latent tendency, called the fruit of manifestation because manifestation habituates it. The English makes the manifestation-fruit belong to the latent tendency, reversing the relation. The opposite case, unawakened, keeps its power without manifesting.

quiz.q: To whom belongs tendency generating no suffering, and why?
options: arhats, having severed all, while bodhisattvas still suffer, the lecture correcting the treatise on this point
stream-enterers; no more hell
form-realm gods; no painful feeling
mastered bodhisattvas; manifestation is suppressed, drawing no result of rebirth
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: manifestation is permanently suppressed, and the seeds of self-clinging tied to segmented rebirth are subdued, drawing no result of cyclic rebirth. So the tendency remains though it no longer brings suffering. Much suffering is of the desire realm, little of the higher realms.

quiz.q: Does affliction-class heaviness differ from formations, and how is that shown?
options: it does not differ; heaviness is the aggregates
neither, being inexpressible
it differs; arhats destroy it, yet the formations continue
it differs, formations being wholesome
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: the seeds of the affliction hindrance in the store-consciousness are wholly severed, yet the present result of past heaviness, the five aggregates, lives on. That proves the two differ. The English is accurate here.

quiz.q: How do the names coarse-heaviness and latent tendency relate?
options: the two are wholly synonymous for all seeds, the question concerning names alone, unrelated to any class of seed
neutral and ripened seeds are heaviness only; affliction seeds bear both names
latent tendency is the wider term
heaviness is form; latency is mind
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: one kind of seed is called heaviness but not latent tendency, namely the neutral and ripened classes; another is called both, namely seeds in the affliction class. Affliction itself is a heaviness, without capability. The English question captures the setup.

quiz.q: How does Master Cháng Bǎi explain force and cause-effect turning?
options: those severed by vision lack force and those by cultivation have it
spontaneous lapsed afflictions lack force; affliction and karma take affliction as cause, as does the result
those with absorption have force
men have force; women lack it
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: arising spontaneously with lost mindfulness, without particular discrimination, such affliction is without force; affliction and karma have ignorance-affliction as cause, and so does the result; this is called cause-and-effect turning.

quiz.q: The English has "A portion of unwholesome affliction in the desire realm has a ripened result." What is wrong with the scope?
options: no problem: only part of unwholesome affliction bears fruit, as §14 and the lecture say
it should say form realm
一分 limits desire-realm affliction; all unwholesome ones ripen, while the English says only part do
it should say "unripe"
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: part of desire-realm affliction, the part that makes evil karma, is unwholesome. So the portion is of desire-realm affliction. §14 says all the unwholesome ones ripen. The English's "a portion of unwholesome affliction" conflicts with its own §14 sentence.

quiz.q: In confused conduct, what are the three views, ignorance, and doubt?
options: not understanding; uncertain; wrongly understanding
wrongly understanding; not understanding; uncertainly understanding
all wrongly understanding
all not understanding
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: these three conceptual afflictions give rise to mistaken cognition regarding what is known. Ignorance simply does not understand; doubt half-understands. The English "wrongly understanding conduct" and the others are literal but correct.
